shared_elements: low-relief carving on weathered coarse stone
stylized face or mask motif with prominent eye/brow elements
horizontal band of repeating incised pattern
monolithic uncut boulder-like block as support
justification: Both show shallow, linear low relief on a rough monolithic stone, combining a stylized frontal/profile face with adjacent bands of repeating geometric and scroll ornament, and the crisp band of squared motifs across B's midsection is broadly comparable in handling to the incised bands on A's lower body. The biggest difference is overall format and orientation: A is a tall upright figural monument organized vertically from headdress to disc to skirt bands, whereas B is a low horizontal boulder whose carving runs lengthwise with no comparable head-to-foot hierarchy, and their contexts (polished museum display versus moss-covered forest outcrop) further separate them.
